transcript.text: Gas oven took ages to light tonight then went WHOOMPH and now the kitchen smells really strongly of gas even though I've turned it off. Is it safe to try again?

No, it is not safe to try again. A strong smell of gas after a delayed ignition ('whoomph') suggests gas has accumulated in the oven cavity before lighting, which can indicate a faulty igniter or a leak. Please turn off the gas supply at the isolation valve (if you know where it is) and ventilate the kitchen by opening windows. Do not attempt to relight the oven yourself.
ok, the meter box is outside by the front door, should I go and turn it off there? the smell is still really strong and I've got a slight headache, I don't have a CO alarm either

Yes, please go to the meter box outside and turn off the main gas supply immediately. A strong smell of gas combined with a headache is a serious warning sign that you may be inhaling fumes or there is an active leak; do not wait for it to clear on its own. 1. Keep all windows open to ventilate the house.
2. Do NOT turn any electrical switches on or off (including lights or fans), as a spark could ignite the gas.
3. Do NOT use your phone inside the house; go outside to a safe distance before calling for help. Please contact the National Gas Emergency Service immediately on 0800 111 999 (in the UK) or your local emergency number if you feel unwell. This is not something that can be safely diagnosed or fixed by an owner; it requires a Gas Safe Registered engineer to investigate the leak and the ignition system.
